title: Module quiz: Tool errors that agents can act on

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent handles returns, billing disputes and account problems with tools that verify identity, look up orders and issue refunds, and it escalates to a person when it cannot resolve a case. The billing system refuses a refund because the amount is above the customer's refundable balance. What should the refund tool return?

options.text: A failure marked as transient, with a wait of a few seconds before the next try
options.says: Ruled out because a rule answers the same way every time: "a validation, permission or business failure gives the same answer every time".

options.text: A flagged failure not worth repeating, with a sentence to pass on to the shopper
options.says: A business rule is understood and refused, and the shopper can be told why.

options.text: A success whose text mentions the balance, so that the model can decide freely
options.says: Ruled out because the refusal must come back flagged: "a business-rule violation comes back with retriable: false".

options.text: A failure marked as a validation problem, asking for a smaller number to be tried
options.says: Ruled out because the amount was valid and a rule refused it: "The request is understood and refused by a rule".

questions.stem: Scenario S3, a multi-agent research system. A coordinator delegates to a web search subagent, a document analysis subagent and a synthesis subagent, and it produces a cited report. The web search subagent retries a timeout twice and the service stays down. What should it hand the coordinator?

options.text: A single line stating that the lookup service was unavailable, and no more
options.says: Ruled out because a generic status hides what the coordinator needs: "The two opposite mistakes in the guide's sample are the generic status that hides the context".

options.text: An empty set of results marked as a success, with no mention of the timeout
options.says: Ruled out because "an empty list marked as a success tells the agent that the search found nothing".

options.text: The failure kind, the query run, partial findings and alternative routes
options.says: The coordinator needs the context to choose a recovery.

options.text: The unhandled timeout, which stops the coordinator and every other subagent
options.says: Ruled out because the other subagents can go on: "a failing subagent must not stop the others".

origin.section: Recover locally, propagate what is left

questions.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent handles returns, billing disputes and account problems with tools that verify identity, look up orders and issue refunds, and it escalates to a person when it cannot resolve a case. A wrapper retries any failed tool call twice, and customers are being refunded twice after timeouts. Which change to the wrapper is best?

options.text: Retry nothing, and route every failure to a person for review
options.says: Ruled out because recovery belongs at the tool: "Recover locally and pass up what cannot be resolved".

options.text: Retry five times instead of twice, with a longer wait between attempts
options.says: Ruled out because more attempts multiply the duplicates: "a refund sent twice refunds twice".

options.text: Retry after a fixed pause long enough for a late answer to arrive
options.says: Ruled out because a pause does not tell whether the first call worked: "A timeout after sending is not a failure of the effect; it is the absence of news".

options.text: Repeat only reads and writes that carry an idempotency key
options.says: "A retry is safe when repeating the call cannot do harm", which holds for a read and for a write whose key makes the service "perform the action once however often it receives the key".
